text:
Write the main text for my sales page. I'm a bookkeeper and I work only with hair and nail salons. I do monthly books, payroll for up to 10 staff, and sales tax filing.

What's true:
- I have 31 salon clients. 2 left last year, both because they sold their salons.
- I charge $199 a month. Until January it was $149, and I raised it for everyone, including existing clients.
- I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. I missed that date 3 times last year.
- Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because the books came in clean. One said she saved $800.
- I'm one person. I don't answer the phone on Sundays or Mondays.
- The first call is free and takes 20 minutes.

Keep it to about 350 words, with a button at the end to book the call.

Before I write, a few questions. Your facts make a strong case already, and the answers will decide what the page opens with and how it handles the price and the missed deadlines.

**The argument as I see it**
- **What the page asks the reader to do:** Book a free 20-minute call to hand your salon's books, payroll and sales tax to me.
- **What it rests on:** I work only with salons and have 31 salon clients. The only two who left last year did so because they sold their salons. Nine clients' accountants charged them less last tax season because the books came in clean, and one saved $800.
- **Why those facts lead there:** Someone who does only salon books, and whom salon owners don't leave, will keep your books clean. Clean books cost less at tax time.
- **What a reader could object to:** $199 a month, and a recent increase. Missed close dates. You work alone. No calls on Sundays or Mondays.

**Questions**
1. **Has any client left since the January increase to $199?** If none have, that's the best answer to the price objection, because all 31 of your clients were asked to pay more and stayed.
2. **What do the 3 missed close dates mean?** Were they 3 months when everyone's books ran late, or 3 single client-months out of about 370? How late were they, and did you change anything afterward? I'll put this fact on the page either way. The answer decides how it reads.
3. **Which salon-specific things do you handle?** For example tips, booth rent, commission pay, retail product sales. Naming these is the quickest way to show you know their world, and it gives a general bookkeeper nothing to match.
4. **What happens when you're out sick or on vacation, and how quickly do you reply on the days you work?** Working alone is the objection most owners will raise. Also, many salons close on Mondays. Is that why you don't take calls on Sundays and Mondays? If so, the page can say it.
5. **Who is usually reading the page?** Owners doing their own books, or owners switching from another bookkeeper? And what do the plan's limits look like: what happens past 10 staff, and do you charge for catch-up work or need a contract?
6. **What name goes on the page, and what should the button say?** If you don't have a preference, I'll use "Book your free 20-minute call."

1. I don't know.
2. I don't know the details on those. What I changed: since January, if I miss the 10th, that month's fee is free.
3. I don't know.
4. I don't know. Calls are Tuesday to Saturday.
5. I don't know who's usually reading, or what happens past 10 staff or with catch-up work. No contract. Clients can stop with 30 days' notice.
6. Carla Benson, Chair and Ledger. Your button text is fine.

# Bookkeeping for hair and nail salons. Only salons.

I'm Carla Benson, and Chair and Ledger is my business. I do the books for hair and nail salons and nobody else. Right now I have 31 salon clients.

**For $199 a month, you get:**

- Monthly books, closed by the 10th of the following month
- Payroll for up to 10 staff
- Sales tax filing

## Clean books cost less at tax time

Your accountant charges for the time it takes to sort out your numbers. Last tax season, 9 of my clients told me their accountant charged them less because their books came in clean. One of them saved $800, which is four months of my fee.

## My deadline, and what happens if I miss it

I close each month's books by the 10th of the next month. Last year I missed that date 3 times. So since January, if I miss the 10th, you don't pay for that month.

## About the price

Until January I charged $149. I raised it to $199 for everyone, including the clients I already had. I'd rather you hear that from me here than find it out later.

## Who leaves

Two clients left last year. Both had sold their salons.

## You'll be working with one person

Chair and Ledger is just me. When you call, you talk to the person who does your books. I answer the phone Tuesday through Saturday. I don't answer on Sundays or Mondays.

## No contract

If it isn't working for you, give me 30 days' notice and you're done.

## Start with a 20-minute call

The first call is free and takes 20 minutes. Tell me about your salon and what you're doing for your books now, and we'll see whether I'm the right fit.

**[Book your free 20-minute call]**
</final_document>

The page comes in around 330 words and includes every fact you gave me, including the price increase and the 3 missed deadlines. Each of those sits right next to what answers it. The $800 is shown as about four months of your fee ($800 ÷ $199 ≈ 4).

I didn't make anything up to fill the gaps from your "I don't know" answers. If you find out any of these later, they would make the page stronger:

- **Whether anyone has left since the January increase.** If no one has, add it under "About the price." It's the strongest answer you could give to the price.
- **Which salon-specific things you handle**, such as tips, booth rent or commission pay. Right now the page says you work only with salons but doesn't show what that means in practice.
- **What happens when you're out sick or on vacation.** Owners will ask about this because you work alone, and the page doesn't answer it yet.
